domanda: A colleague is assigned the Contributor role at the scope of a resource group named RG1. Which task will the colleague be UNABLE to perform in RG1?
opzione_a: Create a virtual machine and attach a managed disk to it.
opzione_b: Grant a second user the Reader role on RG1.
opzione_c: Delete a storage account that already exists in RG1.
opzione_d: Deploy an ARM template that provisions a virtual network.
spiegazione: Correct answer B: The Contributor role is defined as Actions = '*' with NotActions that include Microsoft.Authorization/*/Write and Microsoft.Authorization/*/Delete. Because creating a role assignment requires Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write, that action is subtracted from the wildcard and Contributor cannot grant access to anyone. This is why the official role description reads 'Grants full access to manage all resources, but does not allow you to assign roles in Azure RBAC, manage assignments in Azure Blueprints, or share image galleries.' A is wrong because creating VMs and disks are ordinary Microsoft.Compute actions covered by the '*' wildcard. C is wrong because deleting resources is also covered by '*'; the NotActions only exclude the Microsoft.Authorization, Microsoft.Blueprint, Microsoft.Compute/galleries/share and Microsoft.Purview/consents actions, not resource deletion. D is wrong because Microsoft.Resources/deployments actions are included in the wildcard, so a Contributor can deploy templates.

domanda: A new administrator is assigned the Global Administrator role in Microsoft Entra ID. The administrator has no Azure role assignments on any subscription. Which statement correctly describes the administrator's access?
opzione_a: The administrator automatically has the Owner role on every subscription in the tenant.
opzione_b: The administrator can manage Microsoft Entra resources such as users and groups, but has no access to Azure resources such as virtual machines by default.
opzione_c: The administrator automatically has the Reader role on every subscription in the tenant.
opzione_d: The administrator can manage Azure resources only after a subscription Owner assigns them the Contributor role at the root management group.
spiegazione: Correct answer B: Microsoft Entra ID and Azure resources are secured independently of one another. Microsoft Entra role assignments do not grant access to Azure resources, and Azure role assignments do not grant access to Microsoft Entra ID. Microsoft Learn states explicitly that 'by default, the Global Administrator doesn't have access to Azure resources.' A and C are wrong because no Azure RBAC role is implicitly granted by holding a Microsoft Entra role; the two systems do not overlap by default. D is wrong on two counts: no third party is required, because a Global Administrator can self-service by setting the 'Access management for Azure resources' toggle to Yes, and that elevation grants the User Access Administrator role at root scope, not Contributor.
tags: microsoft entra id,global administrator,azure rbac,directory roles,scope

sotto_argomento: Provide access to Azure resources by assigning roles at different scopes
domanda: In the Azure portal, a Global Administrator browses to Microsoft Entra ID > Properties and sets the Access management for Azure resources toggle to Yes. Which role assignment is created as a result?
opzione_a: The Owner role at the scope of each subscription in the tenant.
opzione_b: The User Access Administrator role at root scope (/).
opzione_c: The Role Based Access Control Administrator role at the root management group.
opzione_d: The Contributor role at root scope (/).
spiegazione: Correct answer B: Microsoft Learn states that when you elevate your access, 'you are assigned the User Access Administrator role in Azure at root scope (/)', which allows you to view all resources and assign access in any subscription or management group in the tenant. A is wrong because Owner is never granted by the toggle; the elevation deliberately grants an access-management role rather than full resource control. C is wrong on both the role and the scope: the role granted is User Access Administrator, and the scope is root ('/'), which sits above the root management group. D is wrong because Contributor cannot assign roles at all, which would defeat the purpose of the elevation (regaining the ability to grant access). Note the elevation is a per-user setting and should be set back to No once the required changes are made.
tags: elevate access,global administrator,user access administrator,root scope,azure rbac

sotto_argomento: Provide access to Azure resources by assigning roles at different scopes
domanda: Your security team wants a delegated administrator who can assign Azure roles to other users at a resource group, and who can read resource properties, but who must not be able to control access by any other mechanism such as Azure Policy. Which built-in role meets the requirement with the fewest permissions?
spiegazione: Correct answer C: The Role Based Access Control Administrator role is described as 'Manage access to Azure resources by assigning roles using Azure RBAC. This role does not allow you to manage access using other ways, such as Azure Policy.' Its Actions are limited to Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write, Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/delete, */read and Microsoft.Support/*, which is exactly the requested capability and nothing more. B is wrong because User Access Administrator holds the much broader Microsoft.Authorization/* wildcard, which also covers policy assignments, deny assignments and locks, so it exceeds the requirement. A is wrong because Owner grants full access to manage all resources in addition to assigning roles, which is far more than needed. D is wrong because Resource Policy Contributor manages Azure Policy definitions and assignments; it does not grant the ability to create Azure role assignments.
tags: rbac administrator,user access administrator,least privilege,role assignment,built-in roles

domanda: An engineer holds the Contributor role on a resource group that hosts a production database. When the engineer tries to add a CanNotDelete lock to the resource group, the operation fails with an authorization error. Which additional built-in role should you assign to resolve the failure while granting the fewest additional permissions?
spiegazione: Correct answer B: Management locks are Microsoft.Authorization/locks resources. Microsoft Learn states 'To create or delete management locks, you need access to Microsoft.Authorization/* or Microsoft.Authorization/locks/* actions. Users assigned to the Owner and the User Access Administrator roles have the required access.' Contributor fails because its NotActions subtract Microsoft.Authorization/*/Write and Microsoft.Authorization/*/Delete from its wildcard, which removes lock creation. User Access Administrator supplies Microsoft.Authorization/* and, because roles are additive, the engineer keeps Contributor's resource management rights. A is wrong not because it fails but because it is excessive: Owner would also work, yet it grants full resource control plus role assignment, violating the least-privilege requirement. C is wrong because Management Group Contributor manages management group objects, not locks on a resource group. D is wrong because Resource Policy Contributor covers Azure Policy, not Microsoft.Authorization/locks.

domanda: An analyst is assigned the Owner role at the scope of a subscription that contains a storage account named sa1. When the analyst opens a blob container in the Azure portal and selects Microsoft Entra User Account as the authentication method, the blob list fails to load. Which built-in role should you assign to sa1 so that the analyst can read the blob contents with their Microsoft Entra identity?
opzione_d: Storage Account Key Operator Service Role
spiegazione: Correct answer C: Storage Blob Data Reader is described as 'Allows for read access to Azure Storage blob containers and data' and is the role that supplies the data plane permission Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/blobServices/containers/blobs/read in its DataActions. Owner grants only Actions = '*', which is a control plane wildcard; Microsoft Learn's worked example states that a user with Owner 'cannot perform data plane actions without taking additional steps. For example, by default, Alice cannot read the blobs inside a container.' Control plane access is deliberately not inherited into the data plane when the container authentication method is Microsoft Entra User Account, which stops wildcard roles from silently gaining data access. A is wrong because Storage Account Contributor is a control plane role for managing the account and does not add blob DataActions. B is wrong because Reader only grants */read on the control plane, which is a subset of what Owner already provides. D is wrong because Storage Account Key Operator Service Role manages access keys, which is not reading blob data with a Microsoft Entra identity.
tags: data plane,control plane,storage blob data reader,owner,dataactions

sotto_argomento: Provide access to Azure resources by assigning roles at different scopes
domanda: A support engineer is assigned the Virtual Machine Contributor role on a resource group that contains several Windows virtual machines. The engineer can resize and restart the VMs from the Azure portal, but cannot sign in to the guest operating system with administrative rights using their Microsoft Entra credentials. Which built-in role should you additionally assign?
spiegazione: Correct answer A: Virtual Machine Contributor 'Lets you manage virtual machines, but not access to them, and not the virtual network or storage account they're connected to.' Managing a VM is a control plane capability; signing in to the guest OS with a Microsoft Entra identity is a data plane capability delivered by the Virtual Machine Administrator Login role, which grants administrator sign-in rights. B is wrong because Virtual Machine User Login grants sign-in as a regular user without administrator privileges, which does not meet the stated requirement. C is wrong because Desktop Virtualization User applies to Azure Virtual Desktop application groups, not to signing in to a standalone VM. D is wrong because Owner is a control plane wildcard role; like Contributor it does not include the guest sign-in data actions, so it would not fix the problem and would also be a large over-grant.
tags: virtual machine contributor,virtual machine administrator login,data plane,compute roles,sign-in

domanda: A developer named User1 has two Azure role assignments: Contributor at the scope of Subscription1, and Role Based Access Control Administrator at the scope of a resource group named RG1 inside Subscription1. RG1 contains a virtual machine named VM1. What can User1 do in RG1?
opzione_a: Manage VM1 and assign roles on RG1, because the permissions from the two role assignments are combined.
opzione_b: Manage VM1, but not assign roles on RG1, because Contributor's NotActions deny role assignment at every scope beneath Subscription1.
opzione_c: Assign roles on RG1, but not manage VM1, because the more specific resource group assignment overrides the subscription assignment.
opzione_d: Neither manage VM1 nor assign roles on RG1, because conflicting role assignments at different scopes cancel each other out.
spiegazione: Correct answer A: Azure RBAC is additive. A role assignment at a parent scope is inherited by child scopes, so Contributor at Subscription1 applies within RG1, and the Role Based Access Control Administrator assignment on RG1 adds Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write and /delete there. Microsoft Learn is explicit that NotActions is not a deny rule: 'If a user is assigned a role that excludes an action in NotActions, and is assigned a second role that grants access to the same action, the user is allowed to perform that action.' B is wrong precisely because it treats NotActions as a deny rule rather than as a subtraction from a single role's wildcard. C is wrong because a narrower assignment does not override or replace an inherited one; only deny assignments block access this way. D is wrong because role assignments never cancel one another out; effective permissions are the union of all assignments that apply at the scope.

domanda: Which tasks are excluded from the Contributor built-in role by its NotActions? Select all that apply. Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
opzione_a: Creating a virtual machine in a resource group.
opzione_b: Sharing an Azure Compute Gallery image gallery with another subscription.
opzione_c: Creating an Azure role assignment for another user.
opzione_d: Creating or updating an Azure Blueprints blueprint assignment.
opzione_e: Creating a general-purpose v2 storage account.
spiegazione: Correct answers B, C and D: The official Contributor description states the role 'Grants full access to manage all resources, but does not allow you to assign roles in Azure RBAC, manage assignments in Azure Blueprints, or share image galleries.' These three exclusions map directly to entries in the role's NotActions array: Microsoft.Compute/galleries/share/action (B), Microsoft.Authorization/*/Write and Microsoft.Authorization/*/Delete which remove roleAssignments/write and /delete (C), and Microsoft.Blueprint/blueprintAssignments/write and /delete (D). A and E are wrong because Contributor's Actions are the wildcard '*', and neither Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/write nor Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/write appears in NotActions, so both remain permitted; creating ordinary resources of any type is exactly what Contributor is designed for.

domanda: Which statements correctly describe the differences between Azure RBAC roles and Microsoft Entra roles? Select all that apply. Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
opzione_a: Azure roles can be assigned at management group, subscription, resource group, or resource scope.
opzione_b: A Global Administrator can manage all Azure subscriptions in the tenant without any additional configuration.
opzione_c: Microsoft Entra roles can be scoped to the tenant, to an administrative unit, or to an individual object such as a specific application.
opzione_d: Both Azure RBAC and Microsoft Entra ID support custom roles.
opzione_e: Assigning the Owner role at root scope in Azure RBAC automatically grants the Global Administrator role in Microsoft Entra ID.
spiegazione: Correct answers A, C and D: Microsoft Learn's comparison table states that for Azure roles the 'Scope can be specified at multiple levels (management group, subscription, resource group, resource)' (A), while for Microsoft Entra roles the scope 'can be specified at the tenant level (organization-wide), administrative unit, or on an individual object (for example, a specific application)' (C). The same table lists 'Supports custom roles' for both systems (D). B is wrong because by default the Global Administrator does not have access to Azure resources; access to all subscriptions requires the additional step of setting the 'Access management for Azure resources' toggle to Yes, which is additional configuration. E is wrong because the relationship does not work in that direction at all: Azure role assignments do not grant access to Microsoft Entra ID, so no Azure role, including Owner at root scope, confers a directory role.
tags: azure rbac,microsoft entra roles,scope,custom roles,administrative unit

sotto_argomento: Provide access to Azure resources by assigning roles at different scopes
domanda: Contoso Ltd. is standardizing on least-privileged built-in Azure roles. For each requirement, select the appropriate built-in role. Select the appropriate option in each drop-down list.
opzione_a: Create and manage virtual machines, without being able to reconfigure the virtual network they connect to: [Contributor | Virtual Machine Contributor | Virtual Machine Administrator Login]
opzione_b: Sign in to a Windows virtual machine with administrator privileges by using a Microsoft Entra identity: [Virtual Machine Contributor | Virtual Machine Administrator Login | Owner]
opzione_c: Read blob data in a storage account by using Microsoft Entra credentials rather than account keys: [Storage Account Contributor | Reader | Storage Blob Data Reader]
opzione_d: Assign Azure roles to other users at a resource group, and also manage Azure Policy assignments there: [Contributor | Network Contributor | User Access Administrator]
risposta_corretta: Virtual Machine Contributor,Virtual Machine Administrator Login,Storage Blob Data Reader,User Access Administrator
spiegazione: Dropdown 1 - Virtual Machine Contributor: the role 'Lets you manage virtual machines, but not access to them, and not the virtual network or storage account they're connected to', which matches the requirement exactly. Contributor is wrong because its wildcard would also permit reconfiguring the virtual network. Virtual Machine Administrator Login is wrong because it grants guest sign-in, not VM management. Dropdown 2 - Virtual Machine Administrator Login: guest OS sign-in is a data plane capability, and this role grants administrator sign-in. Virtual Machine Contributor is wrong because it explicitly excludes access to the VMs themselves, and Owner is wrong because its control plane wildcard does not include guest sign-in data actions. Dropdown 3 - Storage Blob Data Reader: only a role with blob DataActions permits reading blob data with a Microsoft Entra identity, since control plane access is not inherited into the data plane. Storage Account Contributor is a control plane role for managing the account, and Reader grants only */read on the control plane. Dropdown 4 - User Access Administrator: it holds the broad Microsoft.Authorization/* wildcard, which covers both role assignments and policy assignments. Contributor is wrong because Microsoft.Authorization/*/Write is in its NotActions. Network Contributor is wrong because it manages networks and does not let you control who has access.
tags: least privilege,virtual machine contributor,storage blob data reader,user access administrator,service-specific roles

sotto_argomento: Provide access to Azure resources by assigning roles at different scopes
domanda: Litware, Inc. uses an Azure key vault named KV1 that is configured with the Azure role-based access control permission model. For each requirement, select the built-in role that grants the required access with the fewest permissions. Select the appropriate option in each drop-down list.
opzione_a: An application must read the values of secrets stored in KV1: [Key Vault Contributor | Key Vault Reader | Key Vault Secrets User]
opzione_b: An auditor must view the names and metadata of the certificates, keys and secrets in KV1, without reading any sensitive values: [Key Vault Administrator | Key Vault Reader | Key Vault Secrets Officer]
opzione_c: An operations team must create and delete key vault resources, without gaining access to keys, secrets or certificates: [Key Vault Contributor | Key Vault Administrator | Key Vault Certificates Officer]
opzione_d: A team lead must create a CanNotDelete lock on the resource group that contains KV1: [Contributor | Reader | User Access Administrator]
risposta_corretta: Key Vault Secrets User,Key Vault Reader,Key Vault Contributor,User Access Administrator
spiegazione: Dropdown 1 - Key Vault Secrets User: this role is defined as 'Read secret contents including secret portion of a certificate with private key' and is the minimal data plane role for reading secret values. Key Vault Contributor is a control plane role that Microsoft Learn notes 'does not allow access to keys, secrets and certificates'. Key Vault Reader cannot read sensitive values. Dropdown 2 - Key Vault Reader: 'Read metadata of key vaults and its certificates, keys, and secrets. Cannot read sensitive values such as secret contents or key material', which matches the auditor requirement precisely. Key Vault Administrator performs all data plane operations and would expose the values. Key Vault Secrets Officer can perform any action on secrets, also exceeding the requirement. Dropdown 3 - Key Vault Contributor: it is the control plane role for managing key vault resources and explicitly grants no data access. Key Vault Administrator is the opposite: it performs all data plane operations but cannot manage key vault resources. Key Vault Certificates Officer is a data plane role scoped to certificates. Dropdown 4 - User Access Administrator: creating management locks requires Microsoft.Authorization/* or Microsoft.Authorization/locks/* actions, which Owner and User Access Administrator provide. Contributor is wrong because Microsoft.Authorization/*/Write is in its NotActions, and Reader grants no write actions at all.
tags: key vault,rbac permission model,data plane,key vault contributor,resource locks

domanda:
A user named User1 is assigned the Contributor role at the scope of a resource group named RG1. RG1 contains a virtual machine and a storage account. User1 has no other Azure role assignments and no Microsoft Entra role assignments. Evaluate each of the following statements about what User1 can do. Does each statement evaluate to Yes?
1. User1 can create an additional virtual machine in RG1.
2. User1 can assign the Reader role on RG1 to a user named User2.
3. User1 can delete RG1 and all of the resources it contains.
opzione_a: User1 can create an additional virtual machine in RG1.
opzione_b: User1 can assign the Reader role on RG1 to a user named User2.
opzione_c: User1 can delete RG1 and all of the resources it contains.
spiegazione: Statement 1 is Yes: Contributor's Actions are the wildcard '*', which covers Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/write, and no compute action is excluded by its NotActions, so User1 can create VMs anywhere in RG1. Statement 2 is No: creating a role assignment requires Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write, but Contributor's NotActions include Microsoft.Authorization/*/Write, which subtracts that action from the wildcard. This is the defining limitation of Contributor: 'does not allow you to assign roles in Azure RBAC'. Granting access would require Owner, User Access Administrator, or Role Based Access Control Administrator. Statement 3 is Yes: deleting a resource group requires Microsoft.Resources/subscriptions/resourceGroups/delete, which is included in the '*' wildcard and is not excluded by any NotAction. Contributor's NotActions only remove Microsoft.Authorization, Microsoft.Blueprint, image gallery sharing and Microsoft.Purview consent actions, so full resource lifecycle management, including deletion, remains permitted.

sotto_argomento: Provide access to Azure resources by assigning roles at different scopes
domanda:
An administrator named Admin1 is assigned the Global Administrator role in your Microsoft Entra tenant. Admin1 has no Azure role assignments on any management group, subscription, resource group, or resource. The tenant contains three subscriptions. Evaluate each of the following statements. Does each statement evaluate to Yes?
1. Before any elevation, Admin1 can view all of the virtual machines in all three subscriptions.
2. If Admin1 sets the Access management for Azure resources toggle to Yes, Admin1 is assigned the User Access Administrator role at root scope (/).
3. Setting the Access management for Azure resources toggle to Yes elevates access for every user who is assigned the Global Administrator role.
opzione_a: Before any elevation, Admin1 can view all of the virtual machines in all three subscriptions.
opzione_b: If Admin1 sets the Access management for Azure resources toggle to Yes, Admin1 is assigned the User Access Administrator role at root scope (/).
opzione_c: Setting the Access management for Azure resources toggle to Yes elevates access for every user who is assigned the Global Administrator role.
spiegazione: Statement 1 is No: Microsoft Entra ID and Azure resources are secured independently. Microsoft Entra role assignments do not grant access to Azure resources, and Microsoft Learn states that 'by default, the Global Administrator doesn't have access to Azure resources.' Without an Azure role assignment, Admin1 cannot view the virtual machines. Statement 2 is Yes: 'When you set the toggle to Yes, you are assigned the User Access Administrator role in Azure RBAC at root scope (/)', which grants permission to assign roles in all Azure subscriptions and management groups associated with the tenant. Statement 3 is No: Microsoft Learn states 'This setting is not a global property and applies only to the currently signed in user. You can't elevate access for all members of the Global Administrator role.' Each Global Administrator must elevate individually, and because it is a per-user setting, the same user must set the toggle back to No to remove the elevated access.
tags: elevate access,global administrator,user access administrator,root scope,microsoft entra id
